resources.name: RAINN National Sexual Assault Hotline
resources.description: Talk by phone, text or online chat with a trained staff member who supports survivors of sexual violence and their loved ones.
resources.notes: rainn.org blocked automated fetches (HTTP 403). Details come from search results showing rainn.org text; phone also matches the CDC page. Chat URL varies on some old pages (hotline.rainn.org); rainn.org/hotline is the one on current pages. Spanish options include chat and WhatsApp.

resources.name: 1in6
resources.hours: Weekly online sessions, about 1 hour each, several evenings and one midday per week (Eastern and Pacific times listed on site)
resources.description: Free, counselor-facilitated text-based online support groups for men 18 and older who experienced sexual abuse or assault. Peer support, not therapy or crisis service.
resources.notes: No phone line. Site refers one-to-one help to the RAINN hotline. Languages not stated. Chat URL is the landing page; the group sign-up link was not confirmed.

resources.name: DoD Safe Helpline
resources.description: Support by phone and online chat for members of the Department of Defense community and their loved ones affected by sexual assault.
resources.notes: Phone read on site; hours, cost, languages and text option not stated on the page fetched. Serves the military community specifically (service members and families), so community is approximate. Chat link was named on site, exact URL not confirmed.

resources.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
resources.languages: English and Spanish (Spanish site at espanol.thehotline.org)
resources.description: Call, text or chat with an advocate about domestic violence, safety planning and local resources.
resources.notes: Site warns of longer waits at times. TTY and videophone options exist; Deaf videophone is 855-812-1001 (see separate entry). Other languages by interpreter not confirmed on page.

resources.name: National Domestic Violence Hotline: Deaf Hotline
resources.description: A videophone line for Deaf and hard of hearing people to reach an advocate about domestic violence.
resources.notes: Number read on thehotline.org homepage as a separate Deaf Hotline videophone line. Hours not confirmed on the official site (a third-party search summary said weekday daytime Pacific time). The dedicated Deaf page URL tried returned 404. Confirm hours before publishing.

resources.name: love is respect
resources.description: Phone, text and live chat support for teens and young adults about dating abuse and unhealthy relationships, plus information for friends and family.
resources.notes: Phone and text read on site. Hours and cost not stated on the page fetched (URL suggests 24/7 but not confirmed). Chat link points to the landing page.

resources.name: Peaceful Families Project
resources.description: A Muslim-focused nonprofit offering domestic violence toolkits and a directory that connects survivors with domestic violence organizations and shelters across the US and Canada.
resources.notes: Site is current (2025 annual report, 2026 events). No crisis hotline. Only an office line, (540) 324-8818, which is not a crisis line, so phone left blank. Page does not say whether the directory is Muslim-specific.

resources.name: HEART (Health, Education, Advocacy, Research and Training)
resources.description: A Chicago-based nonprofit offering faith-informed sexual health and violence education and a Get Support section for Muslim communities.
resources.notes: Site is current (copyright 2026). No helpline or phone listed. The Get Support subpages (Am I experiencing violence or harm, Additional Resources) were not read in detail.

resources.name: Tahirih Justice Center
resources.description: Free legal services and case management for immigrant women, girls and survivors of gender-based violence, with offices in VA, GA, MD, TX and CA.
resources.notes: Phone read on site for case help. Hours and staff languages not stated. Social services cost not stated. Services are provided through five offices, not remotely everywhere.

resources.name: Esperanza United
resources.description: A national resource center for Latin@ communities with a directory of national and local organizations and guides on domestic and sexual violence.
resources.notes: esperanzaunited.org blocked direct fetch (403); read via search results showing the site's own pages. Its 24-hour bilingual crisis line, 651-772-1611, serves Minnesota callers, so phone left blank for a national listing. Elsewhere the site points to the National Domestic Violence Hotline.

resources.name: WomensLaw.org Email Hotline
resources.description: Free-to-read US legal information on domestic violence, sexual assault and stalking, with an email hotline answered by attorneys. It gives legal information, not legal advice.
resources.notes: Email Hotline is closed to new users until Thursday, November 12, 2026 at 9AM ET (returning users can log in). Cost of the hotline not stated on the hotline page; main site is free to read. womenslaw.org itself returned 403. It does not take phone calls.

resources.name: National Human Trafficking Hotline
resources.description: Confidential phone, text and chat help for victims and survivors of human trafficking and people who suspect trafficking.
resources.notes: TTY 711. Cost not stated on page (carrier rates may apply to texts). Staff languages not stated.

resources.name: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
resources.description: Phone, text and chat with a counselor for children, teens and adults concerned about child abuse. It is not a reporting line.
resources.notes: Phone and text read on site. Hours and cost not stated on the page fetched. Chat is reached via a Live Chat button; exact URL not confirmed. Call 911 for immediate danger.

resources.name: National Runaway Safeline
resources.description: Crisis support by phone, text and chat for youth who are thinking of running away or are homeless, and for their families.
resources.notes: Site states there is no charge to contact them. Languages not stated. Chat requires a registration page; landing URL used.

resources.name: Boys Town National Hotline
resources.hours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
resources.languages: English; Spanish-speaking counselors; translation for more than 100 languages
resources.description: Counselors answer calls and texts from kids, teens and parents about crisis, family conflict, abuse and other concerns.
resources.notes: Page says toll-free calls; cost of texting not stated. Chat is offered through the related Your Life Your Voice site, not listed here. Email hotline@boystown.org.

resources.name: Teen Line (Didi Hirsch)
resources.hours: Calls 6 PM to 10 PM Pacific; text 6 PM to 9 PM Pacific
resources.description: Trained teen volunteers answer calls and texts from teens who want to talk about a problem. Adult supervision is provided.
resources.notes: Teen Line's own domains (teenlineonline.org, teenline.org) failed certificate checks in WebFetch, so details come from search results and a directory listing, not the org site. Hours are as listed by Find a Helpline; confirm on the official site before publishing. Different third-party pages disagree on the text window.

resources.name: YouthLine
resources.hours: Youth volunteers daily 4 to 10 PM Pacific; adults staff the phone at other times
resources.languages: English; live interpreter available on phone calls
resources.description: Free peer-to-peer support, help and crisis line for youth up to age 24, by phone, text, chat or email.
resources.notes: Run by Lines for Life in Oregon. The old URL youthline.org redirects to theyouthline.org. Its text number matches Teen Line's short code, which is listed on both sites.

resources.name: Eldercare Locator
resources.description: A federal service that connects older adults and caregivers with local aging services, including help with elder abuse and caregiving.
resources.notes: Page says call or send a text message; no text number shown. Hours, cost and languages not stated on the page. Phone also matches the CDC page. Topic is approximate; it is an aging-services referral line.

resources.name: Partnership to End Addiction Helpline
resources.description: Parents and families can call, text or email a specialist to get help for a child or loved one struggling with substance use.
resources.notes: Hours not stated; text and email replies promised within 24 hours. Languages not stated.

resources.name: Never Use Alone
resources.description: A peer-led harm reduction line staffed by volunteers where someone can call before using drugs so help can be sent if they stop responding.
resources.notes: Site lists both numbers together as 24/7. Cost and nonprofit status not stated on the page; legal status not independently confirmed. Include only if the Shifa team is comfortable with a harm-reduction service.

resources.name: Alcoholics Anonymous: Find a Meeting
resources.description: Find in-person A.A. meetings through the Meeting Guide app or local A.A. resources, and online meetings through the Online Intergroup.
resources.notes: aa.org has no meeting finder of its own and sends people to the Meeting Guide app and aa-intergroup.org. Cost not stated on page.

resources.name: Narcotics Anonymous: Meeting Search
resources.description: Find in-person NA meetings through local NA communities and online meetings through the Virtual Meeting Finder, or use the free meeting search app.
resources.notes: NA World Services keeps no database of in-person meetings; local sites hold the details. No helpline number on this page.

resources.name: Millati Islami
resources.description: A twelve-step recovery fellowship grounded in Islamic principles, with in-person meetings in major cities, Zoom meetings most days, and a telephone meeting.
resources.notes: Site active (change log post dated 2026-09-28). Phone is listed for immediate recovery help. Hours, cost and languages not stated. Some local meetings have closed (Minneapolis in April 2026); check the Meetings List.

resources.name: ANAD Eating Disorders Helpline
resources.hours: Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 9 PM Central
resources.description: A free helpline offering emotional support and referrals for people affected by eating disorders. Messages left outside open hours are returned.
resources.notes: The helpline page was truncated in fetch; phone and hours come from a search result showing anad.org's own page text. Confirm on the live page. No text option found.

resources.name: National Alliance for Eating Disorders Helpline
resources.hours: 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM Eastern, Monday to Friday
resources.description: A free helpline for people with eating disorders and their families, with referrals to treatment and support.
resources.notes: Site also mentions texting ALLIANCE to 741741 in social posts; not included as it is a Crisis Text Line route. Languages not stated. Description of services is summarized from homepage.

resources.name: National Maternal Mental Health Hotline
resources.languages: English and Spanish; interpreters for over 60 languages
resources.description: Free confidential support by call or text for pregnant and postpartum people and their families, answered by trained counselors and peer specialists.
resources.notes: HRSA page returned 403 to direct fetch. Details come from search results showing HRSA's own pages; phone matches CDC and PSI pages. HRSA FAQ says it is not a crisis line. TTY: dial 711 then the number.

resources.name: Postpartum Support International HelpLine
resources.hours: Leave a message anytime; volunteers return calls and texts daily, 8 AM to 11 PM Eastern
resources.description: Volunteers return calls and texts with support, information and referrals for perinatal mood and anxiety concerns. It is not a crisis line.
resources.notes: Page says toll-free; cost of texting not stated. Not a crisis line; points to 988 and the Maternal Mental Health Hotline.

resources.name: The Dougy Center
resources.description: Free grief toolkits and education for grieving children, teens and families, plus a worldwide directory of peer grief support programs.
resources.notes: Phone is the Portland, Oregon main office, not a helpline. Fees for support groups not stated.

resources.name: The Compassionate Friends
resources.description: Grief support for families after the death of a child at any age, through more than 500 local chapters and online groups.
resources.notes: Hours and cost not stated on the page fetched; the organization is donation funded. Phone is the national office line.

resources.name: American Foundation for Suicide Prevention: I've Lost Someone
resources.languages: English and Spanish (Surviving a Suicide Loss booklet)
resources.description: Support for people bereaved by suicide, including Healing Conversations with trained survivor volunteers, a support group directory, guides and a clinician directory.
resources.notes: No phone listed; cost not stated. AFSP lists but does not run or endorse the support groups in its directory.

resources.name: Alliance of Hope for Suicide Loss Survivors
resources.description: An online forum and resources for people who have lost someone to suicide, with a supportive community of other survivors.
resources.notes: Site active (copyright 2026; blog posts October 2026). 24/7 forum claim comes from AFSP's page, not Alliance of Hope's. Cost and hours not stated; support groups not mentioned.

resources.name: CDC: Caring for Your Mental Health
resources.description: A CDC page with tips and links for crisis support, finding providers, peer support, basic needs and hotlines for violence, abuse and trafficking.
resources.notes: Page lists many hotline numbers, which were used to cross-check phones in this file.

resources.name: NIMH: Help for Mental Illnesses
resources.description: Guidance on getting immediate help, finding a provider or treatment, judging whether a provider is a good fit, and learning about mental disorders.
resources.notes: NIMH says it is a research agency and cannot provide referrals or medical advice.

resources.name: NAMI HelpLine
resources.hours: Monday to Friday, 10 AM to 10 PM Eastern
resources.description: Trained staff and volunteers offer information, referrals and support for people with mental health conditions and their families. It is not a crisis line.
resources.notes: nami.org blocked direct fetch (403). Phone, text keyword and hours come from search results showing nami.org text; phone and hours also match the CDC page. An older NAMI news item used a different text keyword; NAMI current pages say NAMI. Cost and languages not confirmed.

resources.name: Mental Health America: Screening Tools
resources.description: Free, anonymous online screening tests for depression, anxiety, PTSD and other conditions, with next-step resources. Results are not a diagnosis.
resources.notes: mhanational.org/screening-tools returned 404 and the screening subdomain was read via search results only. Languages not confirmed.

resources.name: FindTreatment.gov
resources.description: SAMHSA's locator for mental health and substance use treatment facilities, filterable by location, services and payment accepted.
resources.notes: findtreatment.gov fetch returned almost no text; details come from search results showing SAMHSA pages. SAMHSA National Helpline is already in the directory, so phone left blank.

resources.name: HRSA Find a Health Center
resources.cost: Sliding fee based on ability to pay
resources.description: A federal tool to find health centers that give primary and often behavioral health care, with fees scaled to income whether or not you have insurance.
resources.notes: The tool page showed only its title when fetched. Sliding fee statement comes from HRSA's get-health-care page via search. Behavioral health availability varies by center.

resources.name: 988 Lifeline Videophone (Deaf and hard of hearing)
resources.description: Deaf and hard of hearing people can reach 988 by videophone, text, chat or TTY (use a relay service or dial 711 then 988).
resources.notes: The page does not say the videophone line is staffed in ASL; do not describe it as an ASL line. 988 itself is already in the directory; this entry covers the accessibility options only.

resources.name: Warmline.org Directory
resources.description: A state-by-state directory of peer-run warmlines, where you can talk with someone before a situation becomes a crisis. Some lines accept calls nationwide.
resources.notes: warmline.org returned HTTP 429 when fetched; details come from search results. One source calls it an unofficial list, so confirm each warmline's hours and area before relying on it. Hours, languages and cost vary by line.

dropped.name: Asian Pacific Institute on Gender-Based Violence
dropped.reason: apiidv.org failed the TLS certificate check (certificate for a different host), so the site could not be safely confirmed. Retry later or try an alternate URL.

dropped.name: Ujima (National Center on Violence Against Women in the Black Community)
dropped.reason: ujimacoalition.org did not resolve and no official site could be reached. Search confirmed the organization exists but not any phone, hotline or current resource page.

dropped.name: NEDA helpline
dropped.reason: NEDA closed its helpline on June 1, 2023 (confirmed by news reports quoting NEDA's own notice). NEDA now directs people to 988 and Crisis Text Line. Not listed.

dropped.name: DeafLEAD
dropped.reason: Not checked; the 988 videophone option and the National Deaf Domestic Violence Hotline were listed instead. Candidate for a later pass.
